subject: Post-call: procurement route & AWS Marketplace interest — next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: procurement route & AWS Marketplace interest — next steps

Hi Jenna / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and to make next steps explicit: 

What we heard
- Pilot scope: 3 internal apps (support search, triage assistant, document summarization) — ~50k tokens/day initially.
- Procurement preference: likely needs PO + standard paperflow (finance approval + vendor setup).
- Marketplace: team is interested in AWS Marketplace (would prefer private offer if it simplifies billing), but finance needs confirmation on invoicing cadence and tax handling.
- Timeline: procurement says ~3–6 weeks depending on vendor paperwork and PO processing.

Open questions for procurement team
1) Do you prefer a Direct PO to Redwood or an AWS Marketplace Private Offer? If Direct, is your procurement group ok with net-30 invoicing?
2) Who is the finance contact for vendor onboarding (name, email, remit address)?
3) Any required contract clauses (data residency, SOC 2 evidence, indemnity caps) we should surface now?

What I’m attaching
- Redwood_Direct_vs_AWS_PO_comparison.pdf (short summary of differences and billing implications)
- PO_template_Pinecrest.docx (fillable PO template you can route to finance)

Proposed next steps
- Jenna: confirm procurement route (Direct PO vs AWS Private Offer) and provide finance contact by EOD Friday 6/12.
- Marissa: will follow up on pricing/quote and provide a DocuSign link for a pilot quote if you opt for Direct.
- Karthik: I’ll coordinate technical onboarding checklist and set a follow-up call next week to align procurement & finance.

If helpful I can also introduce our marketplace specialist to your procurement team to walk the Private Offer path.

Thanks —
Karthik
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_Direct_vs_AWS_PO_comparison.pdf (pdf), PO_template_Pinecrest.docx (docx)

Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement route & AWS Marketplace interest — next steps

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear notes. Quick answers from procurement side after our internal huddle: 

1) Preference: Direct PO to vendor is the path procurement prefers today. Marketplace is interesting but finance will only consider a Private Offer if it keeps our current PO-based process and allows consolidated invoicing.
2) Finance contact: Claire Huang <claire.huang@pinecrest.com>, AP team — remit: Pinecrest Health Services, 1200 Meridian Ave, Suite 300, Atlanta, GA 30303. They require W9 + vendor remit address on first invoice.
3) Required clauses: standard business terms are fine; data residency: US only; SOC 2 Type II report is required for vendor onboarding. We’ll also need proof of cyber insurance limits.

Timeline: realistic vendor setup is ~4 weeks once we have the PO and W9/vendor packet.

I attached our internal PO requirements doc for reference: pinecrest_po_requirements.pdf

Next steps from our side
- I’ll route your PO_template_Pinecrest.docx to Claire for initial review (today).
- If there are specific SOC 2 artifacts and a vendor W9 you can send, please attach them to the ticket I’ll open.

Marissa — could you send a simple quote (line items + term) that Claire can attach to the PO? Also confirm whether Redwood can accept a PO naming an AWS Marketplace private offer if we go that route — that’s an important decision for our procurement team.

Thanks,
Jenna Ortiz
Director, Procurement | Pinecrest Health
attachments: pinecrest_po_requirements.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@pinecrest.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 15:12:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement route & AWS Marketplace interest — next steps

Hi Jenna —

Thanks for the details and Claire’s contact. I’ll prepare a concise quote that maps to the pilot scope and includes two commercial routes so procurement can compare side-by-side:

Option A — Direct PO to Redwood (fastest onboarding)
- Invoice: net-30, monthly in arrears.
- Billing entity: Redwood Inference, Inc.
- Required paperwork on first invoice: W9, vendor remit address, and SOC 2 Type II copy (we can provide the SOC 2 report and certificate).
- Pros: Simple PO flow, direct invoicing, flexible contract amendments.
- Cons: Customer handles vendor management; no marketplace consolidated billing.

Option B — AWS Marketplace Private Offer
- Purchase via AWS Private Offer with customer PO referencing the offer.
- Invoicing: through AWS (consolidated with other AWS spend) — depending on your AWS relationship, net terms may differ (AWS typically pays vendors on a different cadence).
- Pros: Consolidated AWS billing, easier for teams that prefer one invoice.
- Cons: Private Offer setup adds 1–2 weeks to procurement (setup + acceptance); some finance teams require extra accounting reconciles.

I’m attaching a one-page quote now. DocuSign link (shared) will be available — I’ll post the link here once the quote is ready. For the SOC 2 and insurance proof, Monica will drop those artifacts into the vendor packet.

A couple clarifications:
- We can accept a PO that references an AWS Private Offer as long as the PO explicitly references the offer ID and the purchasing terms match the private offer.
- If Pinecrest prefers Direct PO for the pilot, we can still initiate a Marketplace Private Offer in parallel to keep the option open for production.

Next actions (owners)
- Marissa: send Quote + DocuSign link (today). HubSpot deal updated with quote: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/RD-2026-00421
- Jenna: confirm with Claire whether they will issue a Direct PO or attempt Private Offer flow (by EOD Friday 6/12).
- Monica: share SOC 2 and insurance certificate to Claire (today).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
